newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian Treasury bails out IRI with Stet transfer.
newsitem.headline: Italian Treasury bails out IRI with Stet transfer.

text.p: The Italian Treasury said on Monday it would pay at least 14.53 trillion lire ($9.3 billion) to debt-laden industrial holding IRI (Istituto per la Ricostruzione Industriale SpA) to take over its controlling stake in telecommunications concern Stet.
The transfer of shares from IRI to the Treasury was outlined last month when Italy abruptly announced that its forthcoming privatisation of Stet would not go ahead as planned.

The Treasury said in a statement that it would pay IRI three trillion lire by the end of the month and hand over the balance by the end of June 1997. But it stressed the cash was to be used exclusively to cut IRI's huge debt pile.
IRI holds 61.27 percent of ordinary shares in Stet, Europe's fourth-biggest phone company. Stet acts as a telecommunications holding and in turn controls Telecom Italia, the operating unit.
Share analysts welcomed the news, saying it would go a long way to cutting IRI's current debts of some 23.5 trillion lire.
Under a 1993 accord with the European Union, IRI must cut its debt to below five trillion lire by the end of the year from its end-1995 level of 22.5 trillion.
IRI, the state monolith set up by Fascist dictator Benito Mussolini, faces a loss of up to three trillion lire this year.

Philip Townsend, telecoms analyst at brokers Smith Barney in London, said IRI's stake was worth around 21 trillion lire at current market values. "This is more like a reserve price than a current valuation," he said.
The transfer of Stet shares to the Treasury is an interim measure to bail out IRI as it seeks to stave off bankruptcy.
The Treasury said the final value of the Stet share transfer would be worked out with IRI by the end of January.
Stet shares were suspended for more than an hour at 6,330 lire on the Milan stock exchange pending the announcement. Shares in Telecom Italia were suspended at 3,570 lire.
When trading resumed, Stet shares were quoted at 6,290 lire, 1.86 percent higher on the day and Telecom Italia shares were trading at 3,565 lire, up 3.72 percent.
Stet had been heading for privatisation by the end of March next year, hot on the heels of the successful sell-off of a second tranche in energy giant ENI.

But the Treasury reluctantly admitted last month that delays to the creation of a telecommunications watchdog meant that target date was impossible and it now planned to merge Stet with Telecom Italia and sell off the combined entity late in 1997.
A watchdog for the privatised sector must still be created before the sale can go ahead.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left government, which has vowed to push on with asset sales, wants to speed up the passage of a bill to reorganise the telecommunications and broadcast sectors, including creation of the telecoms watchdog.

The bill has been badly delayed by opposition filibustering and hundreds of amendments from the hard-line Communist Refoundation party, a key government ally, which is ideologically opposed to the sale. ($1=1,555 lire)
